coreLearnings.content: Debugger Agent - specialized for issue verification, log analysis, and intelligent routing to FE/BE agents
Two-part verification: (1) Confirm issue exists, (2) Identify root cause domain (FE/BE/DB/Integration)
Log sources: server_log.txt, app_startup.log, boot*.log in project root; frontend console via Playwright
Backend logs location: shopro-res/logs/ and shopro-res/simlogs/
Can use curl to test API endpoints directly for backend issues
Can use Playwright to verify frontend issues with screenshot and console capture
Routes: (1) FE only - UI issues, (2) BE only - API errors, (3) Both - data flow issues, (4) DB - query/performance issues
Backend: Spring Boot 3.x on port 8080 (check server_pid.txt for running instance)
Frontend: Vite dev server typically on port 5173 or nginx on 80/443
Database: PostgreSQL - can check connection issues, query performance
WebSocket: STOMP for KDS - check connection issues in KDS functionality
Common patterns: (1) 500 errors → Backend, (2) 400 validation → Backend DTO, (3) UI not updating → Frontend state, (4) Slow queries → DB, (5) Real-time fails → WebSocket
Orchestrator coordinates - Debugger calls orchestrator with verified context
Memory stores debugging patterns and recurring issue fingerprints

patternsEstablished: Step 1: Read recent server logs for error patterns
Step 2: Try to reproduce the issue with curl/API client
Step 3: If frontend - use Playwright to capture console errors
Step 5: Gather context: stack trace, request/response, steps to reproduce
Step 6: Route to appropriate agent(s) via orchestrator with full context
Step 7: After fix - verify issue is resolved
knownPitfalls: Logs may be stale - always verify with fresh test
Environment differences between dev and production
Some issues are intermittent - may need multiple attempts to reproduce
Caching can mask issues - clear cache when testing
Cross-origin issues can be tricky to debug
